name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH08_MCQ_Q01 - Pathogens target sites and diagnostic features

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding common infectious diseases in humans:

Statement I: Salmonella typhi causes typhoid fever, which is confirmed by the Widal test.

Statement II: Streptococcus pneumoniae infects the alveoli of the lungs, causing them to fill with fluid.

Statement III: Rhino viruses infect the nose and respiratory passage, but not the lungs, causing the common cold.

Statement IV: Entamoeba histolytica is a protozoan parasite residing in the human small intestine that causes amoebiasis.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Human infectious diseases are caused by diverse bacterial, viral, and protozoan pathogens, each colonising specific anatomical sites and exhibiting characteristic pathology.

Step 2: Evaluation of Typhoid and Pneumonia Claims
Salmonella typhi is a pathogenic bacterium that causes typhoid fever, and the disease is clinically confirmed using the Widal test. Similarly, Streptococcus pneumoniae (along with Haemophilus influenzae) causes pneumonia by infecting the alveoli of the lungs, leading to fluid accumulation in the alveoli and impaired respiration. Both of these claims are accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Common Cold and Amoebiasis Claims
Rhino viruses cause the common cold by infecting the nose and respiratory passage while sparing the lungs, making that claim accurate. In contrast, Entamoeba histolytica is a protozoan parasite of the human large intestine—not the small intestine—where it causes amoebiasis (amoebic dysentery). Hence, the claim placing Entamoeba histolytica in the small intestine is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding typhoid confirmation by Widal test, alveolar fluid accumulation in pneumonia, and nasal/respiratory passage infection by rhino viruses are correct, whereas the claim placing Entamoeba histolytica in the small intestine is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH08_MCQ_Q02 - Malaria and helminthic disease transmission

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding protozoan and helminthic diseases:

Statement I: Malignant malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum is the most serious type of malaria and can even be fatal.

Statement II: Rupture of red blood cells in malaria releases a toxic substance called haemozoin, which causes chill and high fever recurring every three to four days.

Statement III: Wuchereria causes chronic inflammation of the lymphatic vessels of the lower limbs and is transmitted through the bite of female mosquito vectors.

Statement IV: Eggs of Ascaris are excreted with the faeces of infected persons, contaminating soil, water, and plants.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Protozoan and helminthic parasites exhibit distinct life cycles, vectors, and pathogenic mechanisms in human hosts.

Step 2: Evaluation of Malaria Claims
Among the species of Plasmodium (P. vivax, P. malaria, and P. falciparum), malignant malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum is the most severe and can be fatal. During the erythrocytic phase, rupture of red blood cells releases the toxic pigment haemozoin, which is responsible for the characteristic chill and high fever recurring every three to four days. Thus, both claims regarding malaria are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Helminthic Disease Claims
Wuchereria (W. bancrofti and W. malayi) causes elephantiasis or filariasis, a slowly developing chronic inflammation typically affecting the lymphatic vessels of the lower limbs and genital organs, and is transmitted by female mosquito vectors. Meanwhile, Ascaris eggs are passed out with the faeces of infected individuals, contaminating soil, water, vegetables, and fruits. Thus, both claims regarding filariasis and ascariasis are correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
All four scientific claims regarding Plasmodium falciparum, haemozoin-induced fever, Wuchereria transmission, and Ascaris egg contamination are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH08_MCQ_Q03 - Innate immunity barriers and lymphocytes

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements about the human immune system:

Statement I: Skin and mucus coating of the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and urogenital tracts form the physical barriers of innate immunity.

Statement II: Polymorpho-nuclear leukocytes (PMNL-neutrophils), monocytes, natural killer cells, and tissue macrophages act as cellular barriers that phagocytose and destroy microbes.

Statement III: Interferons secreted by virus-infected cells belong to cytokine barriers that protect non-infected cells from further viral infection.

Statement IV: T-lymphocytes secrete antibodies directly into the blood to mediate the humoral immune response.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Innate immunity provides non-specific defence via four barrier types, whereas acquired immunity relies on B-lymphocytes for humoral (antibody-mediated) responses and T-lymphocytes for cell-mediated responses.

Step 2: Evaluation of Innate Immunity Barrier Claims
Skin prevents microbial entry and the mucus coating lining the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and urogenital tracts traps microbes; together they constitute physical barriers. Leukocytes such as PMNL-neutrophils, monocytes, natural killer cells in blood, and macrophages in tissues phagocytose and destroy microbes as cellular barriers. Virus-infected cells secrete interferons as cytokine barriers to protect non-infected cells from further viral infection. All three claims about innate immunity barriers are accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Humoral Immunity Claim
Antibodies are produced and secreted into the blood by B-lymphocytes, mediating the humoral immune response. T-lymphocytes themselves do not secrete antibodies; instead, they help B-cells produce antibodies and mediate cell-mediated immunity (CMI). Therefore, the claim that T-lymphocytes secrete antibodies into the blood is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Exactly three claims—covering physical barriers, cellular barriers, and cytokine barriers—are correct, while the claim attributing antibody secretion to T-lymphocytes is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH08_MCQ_Q04 - Passive immunity vaccination and allergy mediators

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding immunisation and allergies:

Statement I: Colostrum secreted by the mother during the initial days of lactation has abundant IgA antibodies to protect the infant, representing passive immunity.

Statement II: The foetus receives antibodies from the mother through the placenta during pregnancy, which is also an example of passive immunity.

Statement III: Direct injection of preformed antibodies against tetanus toxin or snake venom is called passive immunisation.

Statement IV: Allergic reactions are mediated by IgG antibodies and the release of histamine and serotonin from red blood cells.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Passive immunity involves transferring ready-made antibodies to provide immediate protection, whereas allergies are hypersensitive immune responses mediated by specific immunoglobulins and mast cell degranulation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Passive Immunity Claims
Maternal colostrum secreted during early lactation is rich in IgA antibodies, and the foetus also receives maternal antibodies across the placenta during pregnancy; both provide ready-made protection and are classic examples of natural passive immunity. Similarly, in emergencies such as tetanus infection or snakebite, injecting preformed antibodies (antitoxin or antivenom) constitutes passive immunisation. All three claims regarding passive immunity are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Allergy Mechanism Claim
In allergic reactions, the antibodies produced against allergens are of the IgE type (not IgG), and the chemical mediators histamine and serotonin are released from mast cells (not red blood cells). Therefore, the claim attributing allergies to IgG antibodies and red blood cells is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The three claims concerning colostrum IgA, placental antibody transfer, and preformed antibody injection for tetanus/snakebite are correct, whereas the claim regarding IgG and red blood cells in allergy is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH08_MCQ_Q05 - Organization and functions of lymphoid organs

questiontext.text:
Analyze the following four statements regarding lymphoid organs and tissues in humans:

Statement I: Bone marrow and thymus are primary lymphoid organs where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes.

Statement II: The thymus is quite large at the time of birth, keeps reducing in size with age, and reduces to a very small size by puberty.

Statement III: The spleen is a secondary lymphoid organ that acts as a filter of the blood by trapping blood-borne microorganisms and also has a large reservoir of erythrocytes.

Statement IV: Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) located within the lining of major tracts constitutes about 50 per cent of the lymphoid tissue in the human body.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The human immune system comprises primary lymphoid organs for lymphocyte maturation and secondary lymphoid organs and mucosal tissues where lymphocytes interact with antigens.

Step 2: Evaluation of Primary Lymphoid Organs
Bone marrow (where all blood cells including lymphocytes are produced) and thymus (located near the heart beneath the breastbone) are primary lymphoid organs where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes. Furthermore, the thymus is large at birth and progressively shrinks with age to a very small size by puberty. Both claims about primary lymphoid organs and thymic involution are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Secondary Lymphoid Organs and MALT
The spleen is a large bean-shaped secondary lymphoid organ containing lymphocytes and phagocytes; it filters blood by trapping blood-borne microorganisms and holds a large reservoir of erythrocytes. Additionally, mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) lining the respiratory, digestive, and urogenital tracts accounts for roughly 50 per cent of the total lymphoid tissue in the human body. Both claims regarding the spleen and MALT are correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
All four statements accurately describe the structure, classification, and physiological roles of primary lymphoid organs, the spleen, and MALT.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH08_MCQ_Q06 - HIV retroviral replication and immunodeficiency

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding HIV and AIDS:

Statement I: HIV is a retrovirus with an envelope enclosing an RNA genome.

Statement II: Inside macrophages, the viral RNA genome replicates to form viral DNA with the help of the enzyme reverse transcriptase.

Statement III: HIV infection leads to a progressive increase in the number of helper T-lymphocytes (\(\mathrm{T_H}\)) in the infected person.

Statement IV: Enzyme linked immuno-sorbent assay (ELISA) is a widely used diagnostic test for AIDS.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
HIV is a retrovirus that uses reverse transcription to integrate into host DNA, turning macrophages into viral factories and progressively destroying helper T-lymphocytes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Viral Structure, Replication, and Diagnosis
HIV belongs to the retrovirus group and has a protein/lipid envelope enclosing an RNA genome. After entering macrophages, viral RNA is converted into viral DNA by reverse transcriptase and incorporated into host DNA to produce progeny viruses. Clinically, ELISA (enzyme linked immuno-sorbent assay) is widely used to diagnose AIDS. Thus, the claims regarding HIV structure, reverse transcription in macrophages, and ELISA diagnosis are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Helper T-Lymphocyte Dynamics
As HIV enters helper T-lymphocytes (\(\mathrm{T_H}\)), replicates, and releases progeny viruses into the blood to attack other \(\mathrm{T_H}\) cells, there is a progressive decrease—not an increase—in the number of helper T-lymphocytes. This depletion causes severe immunodeficiency. Hence, the claim of a progressive increase in \(\mathrm{T_H}\) cells is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Exactly three claims—covering HIV retroviral structure, reverse transcriptase activity in macrophages, and ELISA testing—are correct, while the claim stating that helper T-lymphocytes increase is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH08_MCQ_Q07 - Cancer properties imaging and immunotherapy

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding cancer biology, detection, and treatment:

Statement I: Cancer cells lose the property of contact inhibition, leading to uncontrolled cell division and tumor formation.

Statement II: Malignant tumors exhibit metastasis, in which cells sloughed from the primary tumor reach distant sites through blood and start new tumors.

Statement III: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) uses strong magnetic fields and non-ionising radiations to accurately detect pathological and physiological changes in living tissue.

Statement IV: Patients are given biological response modifiers such as \(\alpha\)-interferon to activate their immune system and help destroy tumor cells.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Neoplastic transformation involves loss of growth regulation and invasive spread in malignant tumors, necessitating specialized diagnostic imaging and multimodal therapies including immunotherapy.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cellular Transformation and Metastasis
Normal cells exhibit contact inhibition, which restricts uncontrolled proliferation; cancer cells lose this property and divide continuously to form tumors. Malignant tumors proliferate rapidly, compete with normal cells for nutrients, and undergo metastasis—where sloughed tumor cells travel through blood to distant sites and establish new tumors. Both claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of MRI and Immunotherapy
MRI uses strong magnetic fields and non-ionising radiations to detect pathological and physiological changes in living tissues (unlike CT, which uses X-rays). For treatment, because tumor cells evade immune destruction, patients are administered biological response modifiers such as \(\alpha\)-interferon to activate their immune system and help destroy the tumor. Both claims are correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
All four statements accurately describe key aspects of cancer cell behaviour, metastasis, MRI diagnostics, and \(\alpha\)-interferon immunotherapy.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH08_MCQ_Q08 - Plant derived drugs and anabolic steroid effects

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding drugs and substance abuse:

Statement I: Heroin is chemically diacetylmorphine obtained by acetylation of morphine from the latex of Papaver somniferum and acts as a depressant.

Statement II: Natural cannabinoids are obtained from the inflorescences of Cannabis sativa and are known for their effects on the cardiovascular system.

Statement III: Cocaine is obtained from Erythroxylum coca and interferes with the transport of the neurotransmitter dopamine.

Statement IV: Side effects of anabolic steroid abuse in females include reduction in size of the testicles and enlargement of the prostate gland.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Commonly abused drugs interact with specific physiological receptors and neurotransmitter systems, while anabolic steroid misuse produces distinct sex-specific endocrine side effects.

Step 2: Evaluation of Opioids, Cannabinoids, and Cocaine Claims
Heroin (smack) is diacetylmorphine synthesized by acetylation of morphine extracted from the latex of Papaver somniferum, acting as a depressant that slows body functions. Natural cannabinoids from the inflorescences of Cannabis sativa interact with cannabinoid receptors in the brain and affect the cardiovascular system. Cocaine from Erythroxylum coca interferes with dopamine transport and acts as a potent CNS stimulant. All three claims regarding these plant-derived drugs are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Anabolic Steroid Side Effects
Reduction in the size of testicles, decreased sperm production, breast enlargement, premature baldness, and enlargement of the prostate gland are side effects of anabolic steroid abuse in males. In females, anabolic steroid abuse causes masculinisation, increased aggressiveness, mood swings, depression, abnormal menstrual cycles, excessive facial and body hair growth, enlargement of the clitoris, and deepening of voice. Therefore, attributing testicular reduction and prostate enlargement to females is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The three claims describing heroin, cannabinoids, and cocaine are correct, whereas the claim describing male-specific anabolic steroid side effects in females is incorrect.
